Programming principles (for this client)
- Focus on anti‑flexion (plank-style) and anti‑rotation (Pallof) exercises, posterior chain and hip control (glutes/hamstrings) and single‑leg balance. These protect the lumbar spine better than repeated loaded forward flexion (sit‑ups) or heavy twisting.
- Use progressive overload by increasing time under tension, adding unilateral challenges, increasing band/dumbbell resistance, or moving to more difficult variations — not by repeatedly flexing the spine under load.
- Train core 2–4 times/week in short focused sessions (5–12 minutes) or add 1–2 core exercises at the end of each strength session as outlined in the 12‑week plan.
- Use breathing and bracing: diaphragmatic breathing, brace the abdomen before exertion, avoid breath‑holding (valsalva) unless he understands how to execute safely.

Safe core exercise selection (start-level to advanced)
- Deadbug (progressions)
  - Start: Deadbug on floor — 3 x 8–10 slow reps per side (2:2 tempo). Keep low back neutral and pressed to mat.
  - Progression: Add banded Pallof press between reps, or extend opposite arm/leg farther; add small ankle weights or light dumbbells in hand.
- Bird‑Dog
  - 3 x 8–10 per side. Keep hips square, neutral spine, avoid rotation. Progress by adding small hold at full extension (2–3 s) or loading with light cuff weight.
- Front Plank (prone)
  - 3 x 20–60 s depending on capacity. Progress: increase time, weight on upper back (light plate or sandbag) only if form perfect and no back pain.
- Side Plank
  - 3 x 20–45 s each side. Progress: raise top leg, add reach‑throughs, or hold a light dumbbell on hip.
- Pallof Press (anti‑rotation)
  - 3 x 8–12 each side. Use band or cable; progress by increasing band tension or performing single‑leg stance while pressing.
- Deadlift/hip‑hinge based core work
  - Suitably loaded trap‑bar RDLs, kettlebell swings, and hip thrusts develop posterior chain and reduce anterior shear. Program these as primary lifts in strength sessions for indirect core benefit.
- Farmer Carries / Suitcase Carries
  - 3 x 30–60 m carries. These demand trunk stability and anti‑rotation control. Progress load gradually.
- Stir the Pot (on Swiss ball) — use cautiously
  - Advanced anti‑flexion/instability: plank on ball with controlled circular motions. Only for clients with excellent baseline stability and no symptoms.
- Copenhagen/Adductor progression
  - Good for pelvic stability; use cautiously and progress from isometric holds to elevated variations.
- Reverse Pallof/Chop/Lift (low-load)
  - Anti‑rotation chops/lifts using cable/band but avoid forceful twisting under heavy load. Use controlled tempo and light–moderate resistance.

Core workout examples (2 options to rotate)
Option A — Quick daily (8–12 min)
- Deadbug: 3 x 10 reps (5 each side), 2:2 tempo
- Pallof press (band): 3 x 10 each side
- Front plank: 3 x 30–45 s
- Bird‑dog: 2 x 8 each side (slow)

Option B — Strength session finisher (10–15 min)
- Farmer carry: 3 x 40 m (moderate load)

Progression plan across 12 weeks
- Weeks 1–4 (Base): Focus on skill and timing. Use deadbug, bird‑dog, basic planks, Pallof presses with light band. 2–3x/week. Reps/time: deadbug 3x8–10, Pallof 3x8 each side, plank 3x20–45s.
- Weeks 5–8 (Build): Increase time and load. Increase band tension, add farmer carries, weighted plank (light) if comfortable. Introduce single‑leg stance Pallof. 3x/week. Deadbug progressions with small ankle weights.
- Weeks 9–12 (Consolidate): Add advanced variations if symptom‑free: standing anti‑rotation chops at moderate load, single‑arm carries, stir‑the‑pot for advanced clients, increased hold times (plank 60s+). Continue 2–3x/week while monitoring symptoms.

How to add load safely
- Prefer external load that promotes anti‑flexion/anti‑rotation (bands, cables, unilateral carries) rather than weighted spinal flexion.
- Use small increments: increase band tension, add 0.5–2.5 kg ankle weights for deadbugs, add 2.5–5 kg to farmer carry or light plate on back for plank only when neutral spine is preserved.
- Avoid loaded sit‑ups, heavy cable twists where spine flexes under load, and fast ballistic trunk flexion.

Contraindicated or higher‑risk core moves for this client
- Repeated heavy weighted sit‑ups/crunches (loaded spinal flexion)
- Full sit‑ups to end‑range loaded spinal flexion
- Heavy Russian twists with load (rotational flexion under load)
- Decline sit‑ups, cable woodchoppers with heavy load that cause forward flexion
- Kipping movements or ballistic trunk flexion that create uncontrolled spinal motion

Coaching cues and technique reminders
- Neutral spine: cue a small posterior pelvic tilt or "rib‑to‑hip" connection to avoid arching.
- Breathe: inhale to prepare, exhale and brace (not holding breath) during exertion; maintain diaphragmatic breathing.
- Brace, not bulge: feel tension through the abdomen like wearing a belt; do not allow belly to bulge on exertion.
- Move from the hips: for movements requiring force (carries, swings), initiate from hip extension rather than spinal flexion.
- Quality > quantity: prefer fewer, well‑performed reps/holds over high reps that compromise form.

Monitoring and when to stop or regress
- Stop any exercise that causes new or worsening radicular pain, numbness, tingling, or leg weakness.
- Regression options: reduce ROM, switch to anti‑flexion isometrics (planks), decrease load, or substitute chest‑supported/core stability drills until symptoms resolve.
- If unsure, consult the client’s physio for exercise‑by‑exercise sign‑off.

- Calories: maintenance +200–300 kcal (≈2700–3000 kcal — adjust to actual weight)
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (~128–180 g/day)
- Fats: 25–35% of calories, emphasize omega‑3s & MUFAs
- Carbs: remainder from whole grains, fruits, starchy veg; prioritize around training

- Fatty fish 2–3x/week (salmon, mackerel, sardines)
- Olive oil, avocados, nuts (walnuts, almonds), seeds (chia, flax)
- Berries, cherries, leafy greens, cruciferous veg
- Turmeric (with black pepper), ginger, garlic, cinnamon
- Legumes, oats, quinoa, brown rice
- Fermented foods: yogurt, kefir, sauerkraut

Foods to limit
- Highly processed foods, refined sugars, excessive alcohol, excess seed oils and trans fats

Supplement suggestions (optional, consult physician)
- Omega‑3 fish oil (EPA+DHA) 1–2 g/day
- Vitamin D if deficient (check blood level), 1000–2000 IU/day typical unless prescribed
- Protein powder to hit daily targets
- Curcumin with black pepper (if desired)

Meal timing & practical tips
- Protein with each meal, 20–40 g post workout
- Prep meals in batches; keep nuts, Greek yogurt, and fruit handy for snacks
- Hydrate 2–3 L/day baseline; more with sweat
- Track symptoms and food triggers if pain/inflammation changes

Core (full integrated safe ab plan)
Frequency: 2–3x/week integrated into strength days + short standalone options on cardio days

Progression summary:
- Weeks 1–4: basic anti‑flexion/anti‑rotation — deadbug, bird‑dog, plank, Pallof
- Weeks 5–8: increase tension & unilateral challenges — weighted deadbug, single‑leg Pallofs, farmer carries
- Weeks 9–12: advanced progressions if asymptomatic — weighted plank (light), single‑arm carries, controlled chops/anti‑rotation chops at light loads. Avoid heavy loaded spinal flexion/twisting.

- Deadbug — 3 x 8–12
- Bird‑dog — 3 x 8–10 each side
- Pallof press (band/cable) — 3 x 8–12 each side
- Front plank (prone) — 3 x 30–60 s
- Side plank — 3 x 20–60 s each side
- Farmer carry — 2–4 x 30–60 m
- Single‑leg RDL / single‑arm carry — 3 x 6–10
- Avoid: loaded sit‑ups, decline sit‑ups, heavy Russian twists, repetitive loaded spinal flexion

Sleep and recovery protocol (rolled in)
- Target 7–9 h nightly, consistent sleep/wake times ±30 min
- 60 min pre‑sleep wind‑down: dim lights, avoid screens, breathing or mindfulness
- Avoid caffeine after ~14:00; limit alcohol within 4 hours of bedtime
- Bedroom: cool (18–20°C), dark, quiet; support neutral spine with mattress/pillow
- Nap ≤20–30 min if needed (before mid‑afternoon)
- Daily recovery: break sitting every 30–60 min; 10–15 min mobility daily; light active recovery on non‑training days
- Morning readiness tracking: sleep quality, energy, soreness — reduce intensity if under‑recovered
- Taper: Week 11 reduce volume 30–40%; Week 12 deload and focus on sleep before testing

Cardio (full integration across 12 weeks)
- Twice weekly: one steady-state (30→45→40–50 min across phases) and one intervals session (20–35 min depending on phase)
- Modalities: bike, elliptical, brisk/incline walking, pool/swimming — prefer low impact
- Progression: increase duration by ~5–10 min every 2 weeks on steady; add intervals progressively
- Avoid high‑impact running if prior symptoms; monitor lumbar comfort

- Progress load when target reps achieved with good form and RPE lower than target; increase 2.5–5 kg upper body, 5–10 kg lower body increments conservatively.
- If any sharp back pain, radicular symptoms, numbness, or weakness — stop offending exercise and consult physio/MD.
- Regress by reducing load, ROM, switching to machine/chest‑supported variations, or focusing on anti‑flexion core holds.
- After Week‑12 testing, avoid maximal heavy lifts for 7–10 days; return to submaximal training and use 1RM data to guide percentage‑based programming later.

Phase 1 sample (Week 2)
- Mon: Strength A (as Phase 1)
- Tue: Cardio steady 30–35 min + mobility
- Wed: Strength B
- Thu: Mobility / light walk
- Fri: Strength C
- Sat: Cardio intervals 20–25 min + core mini‑circuit
- Sun: Rest

Phase 2 sample (Week 6 — increased push intensity)
- Mon: Strength A (Trap‑bar deadlift 4x5; Seated incline DB press 4x5; Flat DB 3x6–8; etc.)
- Tue: Cardio steady 35–40 min + mobility
- Wed: Strength B
- Thu: Rest / mobility
- Fri: Strength C (Heavy flat DB press 4x5; kettlebell swings 4x12; etc.)
- Sat: Cardio intervals 25–30 min + foam roll
- Sun: Rest

Phase 3 sample (Week 11 pre‑test deload)
- Mon: Light deload full body (low volume)
- Tue: Cardio steady 30 min + mobility
- Wed: Light upper technique sets
- Thu: Rest + prioritize sleep
- Fri: Light mobility
- Sat: Rest
- Sun: Rest

Week 12 test day (Fri): follow 1RM ramp protocol for press and trap‑bar deadlift described earlier.

Notes and coaching cues (recap)
- Neutral spine and hip hinge: cue “chest up, hinge at hips, brace” on all hinging movements.
- Bracing: inhale diaphragmatically, brace core, exhale on exertion. Avoid prolonged Valsalva if hypertensive — use brief controlled hold only if safe.
- Thoracic mobility: maintain daily rotation/extension drills to support safe presses and hinge patterns.
- Quality > quantity: prioritize form over adding load. Micro‑increase loads conservatively.
- Communication: have client report any increase in leg pain, numbness or weakness immediately.

Below is the complete 12‑week, full‑gym strength programme for your 42‑year‑old male client (desk worker) with a history of an L4–L5 disc herniation (8 months ago), now asymptomatic. The plan integrates all prior adjustments: spinal‑safe exercise choices (avoid loaded spinal flexion and heavy axial compression), three strength sessions/week, two cardio sessions/week, a progressive core plan (safe ab work), an anti‑inflammatory nutrition component, increased push intensity in Phase 2, a Week‑12 1RM testing plan (safe lifts only), and a sleep & recovery protocol. Before starting, confirm physio/MD clearance and that he’s pain‑free with listed movements.

How to read this plan
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions per week (A/B/C). Cardio twice weekly (steady + intervals). Core work included at end of sessions or standalone 2–3x/week.
- Phases: 3 phases of 4 weeks each: Phase 1 (Base, weeks 1–4), Phase 2 (Build, weeks 5–8) — with increased push intensity, Phase 3 (Consolidate, weeks 9–12) — tapering into Week 12 test week.
- Progression: follow RPE targets and the weekly progression notes. Increase load when reps are completed with solid form. Use trap bar, SSB, machines, dumbbells, kettlebells and unilateral work to avoid heavy axial spinal loading.
- Safety: Stop for any sharp/radicular pain, numbness/tingling, or neurologic change. Prioritize breathing and bracing; avoid heavy loaded spinal flexion (no heavy sit‑ups, decline sit‑ups, heavy loaded twists). Use chest‑supported rows and machine alternatives where needed.

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Base (movement control, technique, low–moderate load)
Goals: rebuild movement patterns, hip hinge, thoracic mobility, posterior chain activation, foundational core anti‑flexion/anti‑rotation.

Weekly schedule (example): Mon Strength A / Tue Cardio steady / Wed Strength B / Thu mobility/rest / Fri Strength C / Sat Cardio intervals + mobility / Sun rest

Session format: 5–10 min general warm‑up + 5–10 min movement prep before main lifts. End with core work listed.

Weeks 1–4 — Sessions (weights RPE ~6–7)

Session A (Push + Hinge + Single‑leg)
1. Warm‑up & core activation: diaphragmatic breathing + deadbug 2 x 8–10
2. Goblet squat — 3 x 8–10
3. Romanian deadlift with dumbbells or trap bar RDL (light) — 3 x 8–10
4. Incline DB or incline machine press — 3 x 8–10
5. Bulgarian split squat (or split squat) — 3 x 8 each leg
6. Face pulls — 3 x 12–15
7. Plank (prone) — 3 x 20–45 s
Core finish (optional): Pallof press 2 x 8 each side

Session B (Pull + Posterior chain + Anti‑flexion)
1. Thoracic mobility + band warm‑up
2. Trap‑bar deadlift variant or single‑leg kettlebell deadlift — 3 x 6–8
3. Chest‑supported row or seated cable row — 3 x 8–10
4. Single‑arm DB row (bench supported) — 3 x 8 each side
5. Lateral band walk / monster walk — 3 x 12 steps each way
6. Pallof press — 3 x 8–10 each side
7. Bird‑dog — 3 x 8–10 each side

Session C (Full body + Conditioning)
1. Warm‑up + thoracic mobility
2. Leg press or goblet squat — 3 x 8–10
3. Horizontal press machine or DB bench press — 3 x 8–10
4. Kettlebell swing (light) — 3 x 12–15 (only if cleared; focus hip hinge)
5. Single‑leg RDL — 3 x 8 each side
6. Band pull‑aparts / face pulls — 3 x 12–15
7. Side plank — 3 x 20–40 s per side

Cardio (2x/week, Phase 1)
- Steady: 30–40 min bike / brisk walk / elliptical at RPE 4–5
- Intervals: 20–25 min (5 min warm-up, 10 x 30s harder / 60–90s easy, 5 min cool-down) — bike or hill walk; avoid row if lumbar rounds

Core (Phase 1 core focus)
- Deadbug 3 x 8–10
- Pallof press 3 x 8 each side
- Front plank 3 x 20–45 s
Perform 2–3x/week (at end of strength sessions or on cardio days)

Mobility & daily habits
- Break sitting every 30–60 min
- 10–15 min daily mobility: thoracic extensions, hip hinge drills, glute activation
- Nutrition: implement anti‑inflammatory foods, protein target 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day. Maintain calories at maintenance or +200–300 kcal if aiming to gain.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Build (increase load, push intensity introduced)
Goals: increase safe strength, raise pushing intensity (heavier incline/flat pressing), progress core and unilateral work, increase cardio duration slightly.

Weekly schedule: same layout. Cardio steady 35–45 min; intervals 25–30 min or 6–8 intervals.

Key change: increased push intensity in Sessions A and C — heavier incline/flat pressing using DBs/machines/seated variations. Trap‑bar and RDLs continue for posterior chain.

Weeks 5–8 — Sessions (weights RPE main lifts ~7–8)

Session A (Lower emphasis + heavier push)
1. Warm‑up + core activation (deadbug/Pallof)
2. Trap‑bar deadlift — 4 x 5–6
3. Seated incline DB or machine press (primary heavy push) — 4 x 4–6 (progress load per week)
4. Flat DB bench (accessory) — 3 x 6–8
5. Walking lunges with DBs — 3 x 10 steps each leg
6. Face pulls — 3 x 12–15
7. Plank 3 x 45–60 s

Progression target (press):
- Week 5: 4 x 6 at RPE ~7
- Week 6: 4 x 5 RPE 7–7.5
- Week 7: 4 x 5 RPE 7.5–8
- Week 8: 4 x 4 RPE ~8

Session B (Pull + Posterior chain + conditioning)
1. Thoracic mobility
2. Trap‑bar RDL or RDL from pins (trap bar/DB) — 4 x 6–8
3. Chest‑supported row — 4 x 6–8
4. Pull‑ups / assisted pull‑ups or lat pulldown — 3 x 6–8
5. Single‑leg RDL — 3 x 8 each side
6. Hip thrust (barbell with pad) — 3 x 8–10
7. Side plank variations — 3 x 30–45 s each side

Session C (Full body + heavier push element)
1. Warm‑up + mobility
2. Leg press or heavier goblet / SSB (if available) — 3 x 6–8
3. Heavy flat DB press or Smith incline press (safe option) — 4 x 5–6
4. Kettlebell swing (moderate) — 4 x 10–12
5. Single‑leg RDL — 3 x 8 each side
6. Band pull‑aparts / face pulls — 3 x 12–15
7. Farmer carry — 3 x 30–60 m
8. Side plank 3 x 30–45 s

Cardio (2x/week, Phase 2)
- Steady-state: 35–45 min RPE 4–6
- Intervals: 25–30 min: e.g., 6–8 x 45s hard (RPE 7–8) with 90s easy recovery on bike or hill walk. Monitor lumbar comfort.

Core (Phase 2 core progressions)
- Add load and challenge:
  - Deadbug with light ankle weight or longer reaches 3 x 8–10
  - Pallof press (increase band tension / single-leg) 3 x 8–10 each side
  - Plank 3 x 45–60 s (add light weight only if perfect form)
  - Farmer carries 3 x 40–60 m
Perform core 3x/week (after strength sessions or on cardio days)

Accessory & shoulder health
- Add banded external rotations pre‑pressing (2 x 12)
- Increase posterior chain and scapular work (total face pulls/chest‑supported rows ~8–12 sets/week)

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Consolidate + Taper & Test
Goals: consolidate strength, maintain spinal safety, peak for Week 12 1RM testing (trap‑bar deadlift and pressing 1RM). Week 11 deload style; Week 12 taper into test day.

Weeks 9–10 — Sessions (heavier intensity but submaximal; RPE 7–8)
Session A (Strength focus)
1. Warm‑up + core activation
2. Trap‑bar deadlift heavier — 4 x 4–5
3. SSB squat / hack squat / heavy goblet — 4 x 5–6
4. Seated DB press or machine shoulder press — 3 x 6–8
5. Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 6–8 each
6. Farmer carry — 3 x 40–60 m
7. Plank 3 x 60 s

Session B (Hypertrophy posterior chain)
1. Thoracic mobility
2. Hip thrust heavier — 4 x 6–8
3. Chest‑supported row or T‑bar row — 4 x 8–10
4. RDL (trap bar or DB) — 3 x 8–10
5. Glute med work (band walks/clams) — 3 x 12–15
6. Face pulls — 4 x 12–15
7. Core circuit (Pallof, plank, bird‑dog) — 3 rounds

Session C (Mixed / conditioning + single‑leg)
1. Warm‑up
2. Deadlift variant speed work or kettlebell swings — 6 x 2 (speed) or 5 x 10 swings
3. DB bench or chest machine — 3 x 8–10
4. Step‑ups / reverse lunges — 3 x 8–10 each
5. Pull‑ups / lat pulldown superset face pulls — 3 x 6–10 / 3 x 12
6. Loaded carry + core finisher — 3 rounds

Cardio (Phase 3 Weeks 9–10)
- Steady: 40–50 min RPE 4–6
- Intervals: 25–35 min (8 × 60s at RPE 7–8 with 90s recovery) on bike or incline walk

Core (Phase 3)
- Progress to advanced anti‑rotation and loaded carries if asymptomatic:
  - Pallof single‑leg 3 x 8 each
  - Weighted plank (light) 3 x 45–60 s (only if perfect form)
  - Stir‑the‑pot or advanced plank progressions only if client has excellent control
- Continue 2–3x/week

Week 11 — Pre‑test deload (reduce volume ~30–40%, keep intensity light‑moderate)
- Monday: Light full‑body (40–50% normal volume); rehearse movement patterns
- Tuesday: Cardio steady 30 min + mobility
- Wednesday: Light upper session (technique for press; 2–3 light sets)
- Thursday: Rest + mobility + prioritize sleep
- Friday: Light mobility and short activation (no heavy sets)
- Saturday: Rest or short walk
- Sunday: Rest and prepare for test week

Week 12 — Test week (taper and 1RM test day)
General principles: test trap‑bar deadlift and pressing 1RM only. Prefer pressing 1RM first, then trap‑bar deadlift (or choice based on client preference). Allow full rest between attempts. Have spotter for press. No conventional barbell 1RMs for heavy squat or conventional deadlift.

Week 12 schedule (example):
- Mon: Light full‑body deload (technique only)
  - Goblet squat 2 x 6 (light)
  - DB incline press 2 x 5 (light)
  - Trap‑bar RDL 2 x 5 (light)
  - Core activation: Deadbug 2 x 8
- Tue: Cardio steady 30 min + mobility
- Wed: Light upper technique day
  - DB incline press 3 x 3 at ~50–60% planned 1RM
  - Face pulls 3 x 12
  - Short core work: Pallof 2 x 8 each
- Thu: Rest, mobility, sleep prioritization
- Fri: Test day — 1RM protocol (see below)
- Sat: Active recovery walk 20–30 min + mobility
- Sun: Rest

1RM Test Day Protocol (Fri, Week 12)
Safety: confirm asymptomatic, physio clearance. Warm‑up fully. Have spotter. Stop if any radicular symptoms.

Warm‑up (8–12 min)
- Light cardio 5–8 min (bike/walk)
- Mobility: hip circles, T‑spine rotations, glute bridges, band pull‑aparts
- Movement rehearsal for tested lifts

Testing order (recommended): Press 1RM first (seated/incline DB or machine press), then Trap‑bar deadlift 1RM. Optional: Farmer carry heavy single (for distance) as functional test.

Press 1RM ramp (example for DB incline press or machine press)
- Empty/small weight: 10 reps (mobility)
- 40% est 1RM: 5 reps
- 60%: 3 reps
- 75%: 2 reps
- 85%: 1 rep
- 90–95%: singles as needed; rest 2–4 minutes between attempts
- Make conservative jumps (2.5–5 kg per side for barbell/machine; 2.5–5 kg increments for DBs) and stop after 3–6 attempts total (including warm-ups).

Trap‑bar deadlift 1RM ramp

- 60%: 3 reps
- 75%: 2 reps
